title: Moving Water Around the City
style: calm luminous paper-cut watercolour science storybook

pages.text: A city is full of hard surfaces. Roofs and roads cannot drink rain, so the water must be carried.

quickWords.th: พื้นผิวแข็ง

pages.text: Under the streets, drains and pipes catch the water and lead it away.

quickWords.th: ท่อระบายน้ำ

pages.text: Canals are wide water roads in the city. They carry the water toward the river.
Floodgates open to let water out. Floodgates close when the river is higher than the canal.

quickWords.th: ประตูระบายน้ำ

pages.text: When gates close, pumps push the canal's water up into the river.

quickWords.th: เครื่องสูบน้ำ

pages.text: Deep under the city, big drainage tunnels carry water fast to the river.

quickWords.th: อุโมงค์ระบายน้ำ

pages.text: Parks and ponds can hold water like a monkey holds food in its cheeks. In Thailand, this is called the Monkey Cheek scheme.

quickWords.th: สวนสาธารณะ
บ่อหน่วงน้ำ

pages.text: Drains, canals, gates, pumps, tunnels and ponds work as one drainage system. They give the water a way out, or a place to wait.

quickWords.th: ระบบระบายน้ำ
ทางระบายออก

pages.text: Across the city, water keeps moving.

quickWords.th: เคลื่อนที่
